method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the 'Rubella' chapter of the Australian Immunisation Handbook, retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- health.gov.au states 'all other rights are reserved'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the Stroke Foundation, Kidney Health Australia and NHFA/CSANZ sources already in this compendium.

claims.claim: **All children 12 months and over: 2 doses — MMR at 12 months, MMRV at 18 months.** NIP-funded.
claims.source_text: All children aged ≥12 months are recommended to receive 2 doses of rubella-containing vaccine. … 12 months of age - MMR 18 months of age - MMRV Rubella-containing vaccine is funded through the NIP for children aged ≥12 months.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Rubella', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/rubella, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Adolescents and adults born during or since 1966 without 2 doses** — especially **healthcare workers, childhood educators and carers**, and **women of child-bearing age who are seronegative**.
claims.source_text: adolescents and adults born during or since 1966 who have not received 2 doses of rubella-containing vaccine, particularly healthcare workers childhood educators and carers women of child-bearing age who are seronegative for rubella
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Rubella', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/rubella, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Women of child-bearing age who are seronegative should be vaccinated** — the purpose is preventing **congenital rubella syndrome**.
claims.source_text: Women of child-bearing age who are seronegative for rubella are recommended to receive rubella-containing vaccine .
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Rubella', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/rubella, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **All males born during or after 1966 — particularly 1966 to the 1990s — should have their records reviewed for 2 MMR doses.** **They are more likely than females to have missed them.**
claims.source_text: All males born during or after 1966 (particularly those born from 1966 up to the 1990s) are recommended to have their vaccination records reviewed to ensure that they have received 2 doses of MMR vaccine. These males are more likely than females to have not received 2 doses of rubella-containing vaccine.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Rubella', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/rubella, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Rubella vaccine does not protect people if given after exposure.**
claims.source_text: Rubella-containing vaccine does not protect people if they receive it after they have been exposed to rubella.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Rubella', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/rubella, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Rubella is notifiable in every state and territory.**
claims.source_text: notifiable disease in all states and territories in Australia.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Rubella', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/rubella, retrieved 2026-09-23
